A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniFlow and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Added content and relocated appendices can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original generation benchmarks, sampling studies, captioning evaluations, and synthetic experiments on three modalities.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds an AudioMAE comparison and experiments on multitask training benefits.

M1.justification: The multimodal flow objective, guidance, transformer architecture, modular training procedure, and inference method remain unchanged. Appendix A.5 adds audio implementation details and evaluates an alternative representation without establishing a change to the adopted method.

E1.justification: The same training corpora and text, image, and audio tasks remain covered. The new VGGSound image-to-audio study examines training compositions within an existing dataset and task, without establishing a new population or input scenario.

E2.justification: Appendix A.5 newly compares AudioMAE with the adopted audio representation, reporting FAD 2.03 versus 1.79. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: New Appendix D compares full multitask training with four-task, bidirectional image/audio, and image-to-audio-only training using VGGSound FAD. It also introduces an audio-to-image aesthetic-score assessment. Existing experimental settings are retained; detailed budgets for the new comparisons are not supplied.

E4.justification: V2 adds focused analyses of audio representation choice and whether training on related tasks benefits individual generation tasks. The existing flow-formulation, guidance, timestep-shift, synthetic-triplet, and failure-case analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The added comparisons retain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: Shared benchmark scores and qualitative examples are unchanged. V2 adds Table 7's image-to-audio FADs of 1.83, 1.89, 2.03, and 2.05 across training compositions, the AudioMAE comparison of 2.03 versus 1.79, and a reported +1.22 audio-to-image aesthetic-score difference.

T1.justification: The flow definitions, objectives, guidance equations, sampling formulas, and Appendix B's mathematical discussion are retained. No substantive mathematical correction, new assumption, theorem, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning any-to-any generation, multimodal rectified flow, guidance, modular architecture, training efficiency, and competitive performance. The additional experiments support existing contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix D interprets the added results as beneficial transfer between related tasks and attributes improved audio-to-image aesthetics to high-quality text-to-image training data. Existing limitations and failure explanations remain unchanged after renumbering.

D1.justification: Appendix A.5 newly specifies AudioLDM2 checkpoint, vocoder, and preprocessing information. The abstract and reproducibility statement change planned releases to reported availability of code, checkpoints, and generated captions; external availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The same 53 bibliographic works and substantive research positioning are retained. Reference-page changes reflect repagination, and the related-work discussion receives only wording edits.

P1.justification: V2 makes limited grammar and terminology corrections, adds acknowledgments, and inserts the Benefits of Multi-Task Training appendix section, renumbering subsequent sections. The main narrative and organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the training-composition Table 7, with v1 Tables 7 and 8 becoming Tables 8 and 9. Existing displays are resized, repositioned, or reflowed, including Figure 12's relocation; their underlying visual content is retained.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful real-data checks of multitask training and audio representation choice, alongside clearer audio implementation details and reported resource availability. These modestly strengthen evidence and reproducibility. Sparse protocols, absent uncertainty estimates, and the unresolved 'Tab.R1' reference limit the gain.
